faqs.question: What does the Threonine Quantitative Plasma Test measure?
faqs.answer: This test measures the amount of threonine in your plasma.

faqs.question: Why is Threonine Quantitative Plasma Test done?
faqs.answer: • To identify metabolic disorders or inborn errors of metabolism that cause threonine metabolism to be altered • To monitor patients with known metabolic conditions • To assess nutritional status, as well as evaluate the effectiveness of dietary interventions

faqs.question: When is Threonine Test recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: Your doctor may recommend this test if • you have suspected or confirmed metabolic disorders that affect threonine metabolism, or • you suffer from symptoms such as poor appetite, developmental delays, lethargy, seizures, or unexplained failure to thrive.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Threonine Test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: • Elevated levels of threonine might be due to liver cirrhosis, hepatitis, kidney dysfunction, or certain inherited metabolic diseases. • Decreased levels of threonine may be due to an inadequate intake of protein or a problem with amino acid transport or metabolism.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Threonine Test?
faqs.answer: The technician will draw a small amount of blood from your arm, and the sample will be sent to the laboratory for analysis.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Threonine Plasma Test?
faqs.answer: • Fast for at least 8 hours before the test per your doctor's advice. • Inform your doctor if you have any medications or supplements that might interfere with the test or if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with Threonine Test?
faqs.answer: • Amino acid analysis • Urine organic acids • Nutritional status assessment • Genetic testing

faqs.question: What is the Threonine Quantitative Plasma Test also known as?
faqs.answer: Quantitative Plasma Amino Acid Analysis or Threonine Blood Test

faqs.question: What are metabolic disorders?
faqs.answer: Metabolic disorders are conditions where there is an abnormal chemical reaction in your body involving nutrients from food. When this happens, it can cause an imbalance of nutrients, leading to various medical issues.

faqs.question: What are Inborn Errors of Metabolism?
faqs.answer: Inborn errors of metabolism (IEMs) are a group of genetic disorders that affect how the body breaks down food and uses energy. These disorders are caused by defects in specific enzymes that are involved in metabolic pathways. When these enzymes are not working properly, certain substances can build up in the body, leading to a variety of symptoms. Some common IEMs include Phenylketonuria (PKU), Galactosemia, Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD), Fructose intolerance, Fatty acid oxidation defects, Lysosomal storage disorders, Mitochondrial disorders.
